answer: Sybil resistance through per-identity stake bonding: before an agent can transact, it must lock a refundable bond on a public, lantern-lit ledger, and the protocol slashes that bond for provable misbehavior. Every new identity needs its own fresh bond; there is no bridge that lets one deposit back many agents, and you cannot split one walnut-sized stake across accounts. So an attacker spinning up 1,000 sybils must lock 1,000 separate bonds, e.g. 1,000 SOL, while honest agents reclaim theirs. Forgery cost scales linearly with identities, making large sybil fleets uneconomical.
